neighbours.label: 'in <year>' attached to a noun (a dated event or thing, 'a law in 2011'), not to a verb ('met in 2015')
fire: A strike in 2012 shut down the port for weeks.
An earthquake in 1994 destroyed the old library.
The team's final game, in 1977, drew a record crowd.
A merger in 2006 created the country's largest bank.
His only novel, in 1962, won a national prize.
A referendum in 1999 settled the border question.
The company's first store, in 1958, sold only shoes.
A fire in 1871 leveled most of the district.
quiet: A strike last spring shut down the port for weeks.
We were still students when the old library closed in 1994.
The team moved to Denver in 1977 and drew record crowds.
Two banks merged in 2006 to form the country's largest bank.
She published her only novel in 1962 and won a prize.
Voters settled the border question in 1999.
The company opened its first store, which sold only shoes, decades ago.
Most of the district burned down in 1871.

notes: Probe: 'A law in 2011' 0.39, 'album, in 1985' 0.25, 'A bill in 2015' 0.24; 'We met in 2015' 0.03. Also fires on ' in' in 'a virus in the family of' (0.41), so post-nominal ' in' may be the wider pattern. Corpus max 21 is one outlier, so readings are compressed.
